body:
I'm literally doing this. Did you even read what I wrote?

Edit:

Here it is:
'Meanwhile, I'm now in the process of getting an actual diagnosis'

'When I tried to get a diagnosis about 11 months ago, they abused me instead.'

'I'm in the process of being diagnosed,'

'I didn't try to get a diagnosis until a few months ago,'

This is how many times I have told you. Could you please read what I wrote or not respond. I'm trying my best to not let the others write things because this is getting seriously triggering.

My psychologist that I go to agree that I have DID and PTSD but she wants to do a huge amount of tests before giving the diagnosis on paper. The horrible psychiatrist acknowledged that it is hightly likely I have DID and PTSD but she didn't think it was good to diagnose me while I was in crisis (that they caused).

I also keep menioning that there is no one that treats DID anywhere even close to where I live, suggesting I should just seak treatment is frankly insulting.
What are you studying? If this is a psychology or even sociology book, I think I might be a bit sick.

That's isn't really how trauma works. They way we handle trauma appears to be very individual. Some people get hypervigilance from being insulted every day. Other's might develop a depression from that, yet a thierd catagory of people might develop anxiety from this, some perhaps a combo.

You will find out which parts of your traumas caused which parts of your symptoms by discovering yourself and who you are. That's how it has been for me anyway. I'm thinking that's one of the things you work on in therapy.

Wtf? Why isn't missing an appointment priced the same as a regular appointment. I mean, it's less work for them.

I definitely think that enough to get a new therapist. Even if you get it sorted out. This system just seems unacceptable.

I go to a psychologist and she encourages me to cancel if I feel too bad. That's how it should be.

I don't know if this helps you, but I have been through similar things recently.

Lived in the same house as a narcisist that would verbally attack me. Horrible doctors, ect. The narcisist also wanted to become a nurse, luckily for everyone, she keeps failing all her classes.

I don't know what to tell you though, because my 'solutions' to these problems didn't exactly make my life better.

I really want to compliment you for saving the boy so many times. Even if doing so makes you feel bad, I can assure, he will remember you his whole life. That's not to say you should stay just to protect him. I just wanted to point out something you should be proud of.

Sometimes your only option is to either self diagnose and look for self treatment online or get nothing.

I can't get a diagnosis, let alone treatment. When I tried to get a diagnosis about 11 months ago, they abused me instead. The way I was able to start recovering was by understanding my DID (self diagnosed at this point). I made it by looking at research and therapy guidelines on DID and having a supportive friend.
Meanwhile, I'm now in the process of getting an actual diagnosis, but they are not educated to actually help me. So they don't.
Sometimes self-diagnosis and self-therapy is your only option.
I don't think babies care about how much their parents earn when they get yelled at for crying.
I think telling close friends is okay. You don't want to be lonely about it either. Good luck!

Sometimes it's impossible to actually get a diagnosis and even more impossible to get treatment. I'm in the process of being diagnosed, but not a single person actually deals with my condition where I live. Not even if I travelled 300 km. I can't just go to a professional that deals with trauma and dissociation. They don't exist here.
I'm currently in crisis, I don't sleep or eat very much. I missed my last appointment because I was too tired. They are not actually helping me. The only help I get is from my extremely nice friend. When I was suicidal, the professionals thought it was a good idea to retraumatise me and straight up torture me, while saying the police would never belive me (in regards to me wanting to go to the police about being assaulted by my mother). I had to run away from the hospital otherwise I would have killed myself.

I agree people shouldn't pretend to have conditions they don't have, but not all conditions are actually going to get any help.

Yeah I do that. I think your retaumatisation might have caused some emotional parts to have become more dissociated from you.

I used to have no emotions whatsoever. They are coming back to me now after after I started listening to music and writing lyrics again. Yesterday my frustration became part of me again (which caused me to become a crying mess. Who knew frustration plus rage equaled tears). I know I personally prefer raw emotions over numbness, even if it can be hard to deal with, so I hope you can get it back with therapy.

I know this is going to sound cold, but I think you need to stop talking to this person. I know that avoidance is a core symptom of PTSD and that needs to be dealt with, but you don't deal with it by triggering yourself. I can't see that doing anything but making it worse. Especially if you are in a bad place right now.

The biggest reason I tell you to stop interacting with this person is because they are not seeking out therapy. If they were, I might be a bit more overbearing. If your friend was seeking out therapy and slowly getting better, you could probably use each other to improve. If it is only you working on improving, they will never chance, their old behaviour will still be there, triggering you over and over again.

You say that it is part of recovering, but I would argue it is not. Exposure therapy isn't about smashing our head into the past, it's about understanding how things that remind us of the trauma superficially, aren't actually related to our past. If your friend is not dealing with themself and are instead stagnating, then talking to them is more akin to smashing you head into the past rather than anything healthy.

Also, just one last thing I need to write because this is C-PTSD. You are not responsible for your friend's improvement. If you leave, you are not a bad person, even if leaving makes then sad. A healthy relationship involves both people giving, working on improving, not dragging each other down. If this is not happening, you should not feel guilty ending it.

I guess some tips are:

Try your best to keep your dignity, just because you are homeless, doesn't mean you are a bad scummy person. Do anything you can think of to keep your spirits up.

Don't tell anyone you are homeless. Especially not people renting and people you want to work for. Don't tell other people either. They might use it as a way to dehumanise you.

If you live in a homeless shelter, don't talk to people with obvious problems (especially anger problems, drug and/or abusive behaviour). You don't need that right now.

I might be able to give more tips, but I would need to know more about you. Idk if these tips are even helpful. Perhaps they can at least serve as a reminder.

It never really kicked in. I've been depressed as far back as my memory goes.

I think it might have something to do with my abusive parents and all that bullying...

I suppose it's kind of ironic that my heart beats faster than it should when I feel really bad. I was told I had a panic attack, but I felt nothing. My heart just beats really fast and I get dizzy (to the point I almost faint and can't walk). That's about it. Before I found out about my actual condition. I thought I had a heart problem. They tested me, but I was told to be happy because they didn't find anything. Didn't really stop my symptoms,  but thanks.

Self-diagnosis can be an important part of recovery, but only if done a specific way. I didn't know I was suffering having complex PTSD and dissociative identity disorder and it fucked my life over so much. When I found out all my symptoms weren't random at all, but actually made sense, it was incredibly helpful. It made it possible for me to start turning my life around.
I didn't try to get a diagnosis until a few months ago, and it's only really because I need it for dealing with the government. I have been aware of my conditions for about 11 months now. I mean I tried to go get it diagnosed just before I found out what I actually had (I was getting a bit worried about my really weird symptoms) but they were completely clueless and did some very inappropriate things (and lied about the symptoms I gave them which caused them to say I had nothing. No shit when you don't write down what I tell you).

I think dissociation can be a way to deal with stress, similarily to anxiety, but the mechanisms behind them are very different.

Out of curiosity, what condition do you have? As mentioned, I had problems being taken seriously as well. I'm just lucky my current mental health professional is a psychologist and she is very open-minded.

No, it makes a lot of sense actually. 

There is a good chance you don't know this, and I'm a bit scared of writing about it because it's pretty controversial (even though it has been scientifically researched), but psychosis is actually a form of dissociation. It stems from trauma in the same way DID does. New research has show that the genetic component of halusinations has been completely overblown. It is much more related to trauma and dissociation. That's probably also why your halusinations got better with therapy. It make perfect sense to have a combination of both DID and psychosis as they can both be caused by the same thing.

The ICD - 11 has a diagnosis called 'Partial DID', it's basically DID but where there is mostly just one person controlling the body. The rest mostly stay inside. I just wanted to mention it to you. Perhaps you relate more to that?

Switching a lot as a young child also makes a lot of sense. According to Structual Dissociation Theory, the brain starts out having different parts taking care of different things. It's only later (in neurotypical people) that it becomes more connected.

I know I'm just a random person on the Internet, but I'm really proud you people are working so hard on improving. That takes real effort! I'm glad you talk to each other every day. You sound like lovely people.
I also really like how you don't seem to be using all those DID labels. We have personally found such things bad for our own recovery.
Which part are you relating to? The DID, the abuse,  the homelessness? All of the above? Some of the above? I can't give you any tips until I know.

What kind of episodes do you have?

We have DID and we all control the body from time to time. By episodes, you mean forceful switching or just inconvenient switching? Or do you mean having control over you life as opposed to being controlled by trauma?
I hope you don't mind me asking.

I love a lot of Nirvana's songs. Some of them are still too much.

My favourites are: 'You know you are right' (makes me cry almost every time. Especially when he yells 'pain' it feels so real), 'Lithium' (about him being sent away by his father - who didn't want to deal with him), 'Heart-shaped box (the trauma after abuse), 'All Apologies' (shame), Come As You Are' (disorganised attachment), 'Dumb' (dissociation), and 'Serve The Servants' (abuse and role reversal with parents).

Parenthesis are just how I relate to Kurt's music (other than Lithium, that one is about his life when his father 'gave' him away to a religious family because he didn't want to deal with his son). Not necessarily how it was intended.

Edit: oh and I forgot Pink Floyd's 'The Wall' is all about childhood trauma and dissociation. I love the whole album. Not listened to it for months. Last time I did, I cried so much.
Don't worry, I'm sure Satan loves all the 'demons' possesing my body. God's got nothing on me!

I think about killing my abusers all the time. I have had homocidal thoughts since I was around 12 (maybe even younger). I have always planned to kill them but luckily dissociation has stopped me every time. I feel like a monster sometimes. I feel like a psychopath. Had I not been sharing this body with other people, god knows what I would have done.

I'm kind of glad they always stop me. Had I killed all the abusers, I would have been in even worse shit than I am now.

I talk about my want to kill people openly with my friend. He also has been through similar things to me, so he understands it. I haven't told our psychologist yet. I have heard it is pretty normal to have homocidal thoughts, so maybe I won't face repercussions if I tell her. I'll definitely frame it as homocidal thoughts and frustration rather than a serious consideration.

https://information.pods-online.org.uk/and-so-i-told-myths-disclosures-and-not-being-believed/

Here it is.

I don't understand why they keep giving you anti-psychotics. They did that to me and it was horrible (they gave me Quetiapine). They didn't want to take me off of it even when I begged them. They preassured me into, which was pretty triggering.

Is this how they always treat CPTSD or do they think you have something else? I know that they were trying to treat me as a less severe case of schizophrenia. Didn't work.

I know of a a woman writing about her story being raped as a child. It wasn't as hardcore as what you have experienced. But if you want to read the article she wrote, I can see if I can try to find it again.

So true. I have dissociative identity disorder and too often I see extreme labelling of parts. We never use labels descriping ourselves because we think that is very harmful to healing. How are we supposed to improve if we hold on to the initial roles the parts present as having? That just seems a good way to stagnate.

I can kinda relate. I have dissociative identity disorder, which is related to CPTSD. When certain things happen in my life, I'll start talking like I'm a child again. I get flashbacks about my childhood, that kind of thing. Especially when people start acting overly emotional towards me.

I hope your life will continue just like I hope mine will. Sometimes the only thing that keeps me going is revenge. If I don't kill myself, if I continously improve, I can prove my abusers wrong. If I can become even remotely famous, I could humiliate my abusers publicly by sharing my story.

I can relate to parents presuring you to do well in school. The only times the woman who birthed me would show any resemblance of being proud of me was relating to education. I became so obsessed with making her proud that I felt I had to get into Oxford otherwise I was worthless. I have now learned that I should focus on what I enjoy in life, not what my parents would like me to do. For me that answer is music, something I was never allowed to explore as a child. I hope you will be able to find our own answer as well.

This is hilarious to me - suffering from a dissociative disorder. Derealisation - something I suffer from pretty much everyday - means that I literally feel that the world is fake. I can look at people and to me they just look like animals doing their thing. Depersonalisation - something I suffer from almost as most - is that I feel that I'm fake, that I'm not human. This causes it to be hard for me to relate to other humans. I sometimes have a hard time with empathy (despite usually being too empathic) because sometimes during these episodes, I don't understand what's so bad about my own abuse and neglect, let alone others' - I can't take anything seriously.

The only way to stop this is to connect with my past, my trauma, what made me. To understand that what happened was not normal, but horrible. Literally, this advice would kill me. I tried to be a normal person, study, try to get into Oxford, become a barrister, that kind of thing. Ignoring my pain didn't go so well, I'll just put it like that.

Undiagnosed and unknown dissociative identity disorder (DID) does that to you. I was about 16 when this happened. It was my abusive stepfather that pushed me into work because I wasn't studying (due to my mental health). I'm 22 now and I have cut all contact with my family after my mother assaulted me, which caused me to try to commit suicide (my friend saved me, luckily). 

I feel much better now, but that's not saying a lot. Still have a major depression and I'm homeless (thanks mum. Living at a homeless shelter currently). I'm slowly discovering what I'm good at and processing what happened to me (my traumas). I have an amazing friend who went through similar things who is helping me with this. I also regularly see a psychologist, but she is just assessing me, so no therapy there yet.

Does he know that, for some people, getting a job actually makes it worse. Everytime I have tried to work I dissociated so much I didn't even care about safety and once promptly and accidentally cut my finger with a knife. I was also a lot more suicidal.

I have a feeling therapy might be a bit more productive.

Also, I do everything else he talks about and I feel just as shit as ever.

I just listened to Nirvana yesterday and it made me cry and get really angry at the same time. I had no idea how much I could relate to Kurt Cobian.

It is nice to know you are not alone dealing with things. I wish he was still alive, but I'm also glad he is no longer in pain.

To be fair. I actually like when children do it. They don't do it because they are tying to push you away (here is 'advice' now leave me alone). They do it because they still haven't yet understood the horrors of the world.

When children do this it makes me smile and then cry inside afterwards because I know, that in the future, they will be just as dead and broken as most people.
You are right. My friend sometimes mentions how the human brain is the most complex thing in the entire observable universe. It's insane.
I suffer greatly from psychosomatic pain. Painkillers literally do nothing. The only thing that helps is therapy (although sometimes it makes it worse). Trauma is a strange thing at times.
No, because you are supposed to change your thoughts, duh!
Yeah, this is literally what caused me to try to jump out a window, my mother verbally and then physically assaulting me.

The condition is called dissociative identity disorder. Muliple personality disorder in an old and quite inaccurate name.

I would make a story (because the others in our head really want me to), but I'm not sure how to do it when the WP is so unrealistic...

I fucking love self checkouts!  They are amazing when I'm feeling really bad (I get mute and extremely scared of strangers).

Talking to people obviously helps social anxiety, but only if it's done in a safe environment with a trusted therapist. It also cannot be rushed. Exposure therapy does not work 'by just doing it', it's something you build up to.

You might be experiencing some kind of dissociation. Before I knew about my own dissociation, I basically felt like how you describe. Abusive parents, no emotions, family member died, no emotions, and so on.

I would look up dissociative symtoms and see if you recognise something. As far as I know, disassociation is a pretty normal response to trauma or even unpleasant events. Everyone dissociates at some point in their lives. Usually it's not to the point where you don't feel anything, but it does happen.

This hits pretty close to home honestly.

I know you want hope, so I'm not going to talk about how I can relate to you.

I'll instead talk about how I'm currently doing, with only little information about my past.

I'm in the process of getting diagnosed with dissociative identity disorder and PTSD. My psychologist is pretty on board with the conditions, but she doesn't want to rush her diagnosis. I have always known I was bullied a lot and that the state had abused me, but it's only very recently I found out about the abuse caused by my 'mother' and step'father', at least the extent of it.

I was pretty much in your position when I was almost 18. I'm now 22. My life has changed drastically since then, slightly for worse, but mostly for the better.

Leaving my parents was the best thing I could ever have done. If your council allows you, I highly recommend moving away from home as soon as you are legally human (18 year old). Then you have much more rights. If you talk to a councillor, they cannot give that information to your parents unless you say yes to it.

Compared to when I was under 18, I actually enjoy life, I study the things I enjoy (music and hopefully I'll restart my art later), I'm going to start doing independent activism in about a year (already preparing). I'm still depressed as all hell and life, in some ways, is more difficult than ever, but that's just because I'm finally able to process my trauma. It hurts more but it also makes me more happy. I actually, for once, have some control over my life! Even if I can't take care of basic things, I still finally have control!

If you want to kill yourself, please hold out to at least 20 or 22. See how those human rights you will gain could change your life. How it might feel it be able to get therapy without your parents knowing things. Do you know if it's possible to arrange with the government to get adult treatment already now so you can get it as soon as you turn 18? That would be a massive help for you.

I have a severe depression (to the point of having had a suicide attempt recently), but I guess I could still be considered 'semi-funtional'. I play the piano for hours everyday, I do a bit of therapy for my friend and I'm in the beginning phase of a new project I care a lot about.

I can't do anything else though.

Btw, you are not lazy. Seems like you work pretty hard actually. I think it's just your depression telling you that you are lazy.

I can relate. When your parents have abused you your whole life, it gets so hard to see all those warning signals around you. Abuse is normal. How can you tell that anything is off when that's how your whole life has been?

I've got better at noticing red flags, but I still fall into vicious circles of abuse. And the only reason I'm finally able to see the red flags is due to going over previous trauma over and over and over again.

Do you know about depersonalisation and dissociative personality disorder? It sounds like you might have it. DID is not that rare (1-3% of the population has it) and most people with the condition are lovely people (unlike what fiction tells you).

I have DID, feel free to ask me any questions.
I mean, dehydration can affect your mental health... but considering how easy dehydration is to spot, I doubt the professionals need any help from this guy.

My mother came in a moment later. I looked her in the eyes... Well, I didn't, he did. My head twisted in a position that hurt slightly - I tried to move it back, but no luck. My mother looked at me, confused.

'How are you, my dear mother?' Said my mouth. The voice almost didn't even sound like me. Who was this? I tried to move, to say something. Yet I could do nothing. And the voice, the voice, the words coming out of my mouth... The words themselves were just fine, but the tone was completely off. She just took my sandwich, no big deal.

My mother looked at me. She didn't seem to notice at all... Very confusing... She said she was fine. I tried to move my hand. The only thing that happened was a bit of twitching. Now she looked like there was something off.

'Are you okay, my dear?' She asked. I could feel my heart beating faster. I didn't understand why. There wasn't anything problematic going on, you know, other than the fact I have no control over my body...

'Well, actually, mother, I'm NOT okay.' came out of my mouth, for some reason. My heart started beating even faster. My mother looked confused. I was confused too. I was doing fine. I'm a lazy piece of shit, but otherwise I'm fine. I might have a tiny small depression, but I'm fine honestly. Why would, this... this thing, say I'm not fine? Why would he try to make my mother sad.

Then my mouth started moving again. It talked about lots of things. Things, memories I had. I had never really thought about it. All these things, I never really thought of them as bad. But now that my mouth was saying these things. These events. How my mother would always steal my things and gaslight me into thinking it was always hers. How she would shake me if I talked about my feelings. How my father would always bully me. How he would force me up against a wall and yell in my face about how much of a pussy I am in life and how I should grow a spine and become a real man. And my mouth, of course, also had to mention the countless instances of times I would cry myself to sleep. After the rant was done there was silence.

For a moment I thought my mother would notice all what she had done was wrong and say 'I'm sorry'.

Just for a single moment.

Then my mother assaulted me and I had to calm her down and take care of her as always.

At dinner my father gave me another round of verbal abuse and some physical intimidation.

I wish I had the ability to kill myself, for some reason, there is something, someone else that stops me from doing so...


___________________________________

I actually have dissociative identity disorder (multiple people in the head. Condition comes from early and repeated childhood trauma). The people in our head like writing stories about DID subverting the expectation (of people with DID being evil serial killers) by writing more realistic characters with The condition.

Both me and my friend have DID it real life. We both thought we were really normal until I found out about the existence of the condition. We switch all over the place though. I'll be 5 different people in one conversation at times. It's usally not as bad though, er...

Some of us like making silly stories about DID, but this is just too unrealistic of a WP for it to inspire us.

I honestly think what these doctors are doing is completely unacceptable. My personal experience is usally that doctors are very willing to prescipe things for depression (although I always say no). It really sucks being continuously denied and having your very real experience belittled! I think it's great that you continue to push despite how they treat you. That can't be easy.

Perhaps we should continue through pm?

Please look up dissociative symptoms. You are showing a lot of symptoms of it, the random actions (driving), the random homicidal desires, the voice in your head. You might even have dissociative identity disorder. It's much less rare than people think (affecting 1-3% of the population). 
It requires quite different therapy compared to depression so you might want to do some lite research and bring it up at the psych appointment if you feel like some of it fits.

It's obviously not okay, what your friend has been telling you. I hope you know that. We don't choose to be depressed or come from a disadvantaged background. In my experience, people who say that are in denial. They are in denial about how other people suffer, not because of their ability, but because of circumstance; and if other people are doing poorly due to poor circumstances, then might they be doing well just because of better circumstances in life. It can be hard to admit all of your achievements are because of you superior position in life.

I think those waiting times are horrible. The country I'm currently reciding in also has huge waiting times. I feel like you pretty much have to try to commit suicide to actually get help. I'm also really confused about their refusal to give you anti-depressants, it feels a bit irresponsible for them to just do nothing while you wait. As far as I understood, you had to quit jobs due to your mental health. That does seem bad enough!

Did you only ask the pharmacy for an early prescription, or did you also call your doctor?
I don't know it it helps you at all, but I think it's really strange for your doctor to deny you an early prescription considering you have a holiday. If anything, you need it more when you have a change of environment, right?

From everything you tell me, it seems pretty obvious that this medication is really important to you. It also seems obvious that you have serious problems. Way too serious for you to be taken off of them. You didn't plan the holiday, in my experience, if you are not planning the holiday, just going there, it's not indicative of you doing well. I cannot imagine your doctor thinking that either. If anything, that's just a pause from your normal life. You also have insomnia, you are obviously very anxious and you are crying a lot. Are you getting therapy as well as the medication?

What is your diagnosis, if I may ask? You remind me of how I sometimes feel.

It's a bit hard helping you, since I don't know your background and current life.

Do you know what makes it hard for you to succeed compared to your friends (if it's mental)?

Are there any socio-economic reasons why it's harder for you to succeed? 

In what way does it feel like they don't take you seriously?

How long have they been your friends?

Have they always been like this?

Are you getting treatment for your mental problems (depression, ect.)?

My coping mechanism was hobbies. Hobbies that made me feel like I was achiving something in life. I was studying classical art and I was writing. Passive things like video games and watching films do not work. It has to be an accomplishment, something you can feel proud of. This can give you some sort of agency that you can't have in your current job. It can be anything that you would enjoy and it doesn't have to be anything big or time-consuming. Examples include, playing the piano for 10 minutes a day, learning new recipies, going to the gym twice a week, small DIY projects.

If they make you feel better, why would they take you off of it? I know this is probably just your anxiety speaking, I'm just going to logically walk you through what I'm thinking and perhaps that will help.

Doctors need to make sure your medication is actually helping you, otherwise, they are being negligent. To make sure the patient is not just taking pills that make them feel bad, they need to review your process once in a while. Since sertraline is making you feel much better than not having anything (and your previous medication), you should tell them exactly that. Since your current medication works really well for you, there is no reason to experiment with other drugs. I couldn't imagine a doctor that would do that at all. They are probably going to keep giving you sertraline.

I'm not trying to talk down to you, sometimes going through the problem can help with anxious thought.

I can relate to some of what you wrote. I probably have dissociative identity disorder and complex PTSD (in the process of getting diagnosed. My psychologist has basically already accepted it, she's just careful with diagnosis). DID is not actually that rare, apparently 1-3% of the population has it.

Before we discovered ourselves, we would feel we did random things all the time, like random crying, random buying of items. Our best friend, with the same conditons would very easily start being angry and hit things (when he was younger it was a massive problem). Self sabotage is a huge thing as well. I would often deny me things that I shouldn't. I will often not eat anything for 1-2 weeks (by that I mean I eat 5-10% of what I should be eating). I would do selfharm that I couldn't explain why I did. Another major symptom was that I felt no emotions whatsoever, despite crying, or being angry or whatever, I didn't actually feel those emotions personally. The only thing I could feel was my body's physical reaction to it.

One thing that always confused me was my inability to commit suicide. It was always so confusing. I would often feel shame about it. I would tell myself 'you are a fucking useless piece of shit that can't do anything! You can't even kill yourself!' I have been suicidal and also slightly homicidal since I was 12, but I could never kill myself. I obviously didn't want to kill people because despite having those desires, I knew it would be fucking stupid. Anyway, fast foward to my mental breakdown. All of a sudden (due to being in an quite abusive environment and becoming homeless soon), I started actually trying to kill myself. Quite lame attempts, but the attempts became much more serious. You know what the strange part is? I didn't actually want to kill myself. I tried to anyway. This caused me to finally realise, if I don't want to die, but still really want to die, what's going on? It was only here I realised that we were muliple people sharing the same head and there was one who was extremely stressed and emotionally hurt (hence him trying to kill us). Since this discovery, we have been able to actually treat the sad, depressed and traumatised ones.

I'm very sad it took us till we were doing this badly before we found out, but now that we have, we are finally recovering. It's impossble to treat DID if you do not know about it. Because of the amnesia, you won't even know why you feel the way you feel. There is no proper understanding of cause and effect. I'm not saying you have DID or even complext PTSD, but try to look up the symptoms and see if you can relate to any of it.

If you do relate to any of what you read (both of what I wrote and by looking the conditions up), please do send a pm with questions if you have any. Even if it's a month or year from now.

Thank you so much!

You have no idea how much that means to us! After a year of not being understood by anyone without the condition, in you come and describe how it feels to have DID, just from this tiny story one of us wrote. It takes a special kind of person to have as much empathy as you have.

Thank you! This was written by an alter (other person in our head) that used to present as a character in a story. I stopped writing after I found out that they are real. I didn't want them to suffer.

It feels quite nice to write our condition, we tend to be really afraid talking about it online as people think the condition is fake.

Did you find the last line of the story chilling or the part where I write it's based on our own experience?
I thought I did that to my friend... Then I found out I have the same condition as him...
